717.t: Synthesizers and his planned eleven-piece band

When it first started happening, especially in the studio end of things, you know it really hurt the horn players more than anything else at first, in the studio. So you’ve got guys in the studio…

437.ch: Views on drummers and the state of jazz
437.q: As far as what I call synthetic instruments, I think the height is passed. I really do. I think in studios, I get calls to do jingles because they want the human factor. 211.t: Technology and the loss of orchestras
211.s: Talkies ended pit orchestras and synths replaced film orchestras.
211.ch: New York Pops and later work
211.q: And of course in film, about twenty years ago went the big orchestras. That’s why you have to thank the John Williams’ and the Elmer Bernsteins and the people who absolutely said this can not be. And it’s fascinating to me now that I go to the cinema and I hear an orchestra many, many times.…

719.ch: Synths, the section and stopping playing

562.s: Drum machines are cheaper than drummers; synthesizer sounds tempt composers to stop developing ideas.
562.q: I think that’s all about dollars and cents unfortunately. Unfortunately we’ve become a nation, even in our arts, of the money-making process preceding the art form. And so drum machines are cheaper than a drummer.

59.s: Synthesizers can help big pit bands but shrinking orchestras are a pity; people have learned to like synthesizer sound.
59.q: Well you know at its best synthesized music can be very useful if you have those two synthesizers as part of the 25-man minimum in New York pit orchestras, they can be very helpful.
